newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan frontline arsenal explodes; no casualties.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan frontline arsenal explodes; no casualties.

text.p: An arsenal at a Taiwan defence outpost facing arch-rival China caught fire and exploded late on Sunday, but no casualties were reported, officials said on Monday.

The collection of bullets and artillery shells on Tungyin, an islet in the Taiwan-controlled Matsu archipelago, burst into flames and then exploded due to the summer heat, a Tungyin military official said.
"The fire was not caused by anyone; it was a self-starting one due to the recent dry and hot weather on this island," he told state television.
The incident caused a temporary power outage on the island in the Taiwan Strait, which is also home to several hundred civilians.
Fire officials extinguished the flames early Monday morning and power was restored shortly afterwards.
Tungyin, located some 20 kilometres (12 miles) from China's southeastern coast, is held by Taiwan as a frontline defence outpost against mainland China.
Taiwan and China have been rivals since they were split by a civil war in 1949.
